transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58m
Recording: (recording available in CRM)
Attendees: Jenna (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lara (CSM) / Priya, Marcus, Daniela, Tomás (Elmbridge)

Summary:
Quick renewal + expansion check-in: Elmbridge is approaching renewal window in May, asking to add EU region capacity and explore private VPC for PHI workloads. Discussed latency targets, cost delta for dedicated vs hosted, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Agreed to run EU benchmarks and share pricing amendment for contract extension.

Topics: capacity uplift, EU region onboarding, private deployment/VPC, SOC2 artifacts, SLA/latency targets, rollout timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Jenna: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I think we had — we scheduled an hour. Quick intros — I'm Jenna, AE, Ethan and Lara from our side.
[00:12] Priya: Hey all, Priya here. We're, uh, mostly focused on timeline today, and what the EU option looks like cost + latency wise.
[00:20] Marcus: Marcus from infra, I have questions about VPC peering and network egress.
[00:27] Jenna: Great, yes. So to frame — your renewal's in May, right? You're currently on hosted plan, roughly 1.2M tokens / month, spike patterns during weekday mornings. Correct?
[00:42] Tomás: Yep that's correct. And product wants EU region for data residency, mostly during EU business hours.
[00:51] Ethan: For us, two main levers: dedicated capacity pools (reserved GPUs) which buys throughput predictability and lower unit cost, and private deployment (VPC/on-prem) which addresses full data control + KMS. There's a middle ground with VPC peering to hosted endpoints if you need lower friction.
[01:10] Daniela: On security, we'll need SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SSO integration notes, and confirmation about customer-managed keys. Is customer KMS supported?
[01:20] Lara: Short answer: yes, we support KMS integration for Private and Dedicated with bring-your-own-key for certain plans. We'll share artifact list after call.
[01:28] Priya: What's the latency delta we can expect if we move to EU region — are we talking 20ms or 200ms?
[01:36] Ethan: From our benchmarks, typical p50 is single-digit ms for EU-to-EU. p95/p99 can vary with sequence length and batching; for the model you're using we saw p99 around 140-220ms under steady-state for 8k seq; but that depends on batch size and KV cache hit rate. We'll run a tailored run for Elmbridge.
[01:56] Marcus: Okay but how about the dedicated capacity spin up time? We cannot tolerate long lead times in May — product needs it live before the 15th.
[02:03] Jenna: We can provision dedicated pools in 7-12 business days typically if capacity is available in region. EU sometimes needs 10-14 days depending on GPU availability. We can prioritize with a commitment.
[02:14] Tomás: So a contract extension + committed capacity would be the fastest?
[02:19] Jenna: Exactly — a short term amendment for committed capacity gets you priority provisioning and a better rate.
[02:25] Priya: And if we go with private deployment, what's the timeline?
[02:29] Ethan: Private (VPC private control plane or on-prem package) has more setup: network handshakes, KMS work, and possibly our onsite install — typically 4–6 weeks for EU on-prem pilot. VPC peering with hosted is faster, 1–2 weeks for peering + routing testing.
[02:47] Daniela: For legal we need data retention guarantees and audit logs. Are audit logs available for both Dedicated and Private?
[02:52] Lara: Yes, audit logs and extended retention are available as add-ons. We'll include the retention tiers and costs in the artifact bundle.
[02:59] Priya: Cost question — how much more is EU dedicated compared to hosted? Rough ballpark.
[03:05] Jenna: Ballpark: dedicated committed capacity can reduce per-token cost by 15–30% depending on utilization, but region uplift and reserved commitment will change out-of-the-box pricing. We'll send an itemized comparison for your current usage pattern.
[03:17] Marcus: Any blockers on network side — public IPs, NAT, firewall rules?
[03:21] Ethan: We typically use VPC peering and no public IPs for private. For dedicated, endpoints can be private within our managed infra; you'll need specific CIDR ranges and certain outbound rules for telemetry.
[03:36] Tomás: Are there examples of other healthcare customers who did EU private deployment?
[03:41] Lara: Yes, we have a short case note — I'll share a sanitized reference and timeline.
[03:45] Priya: For the benchmark, can you run tests with our typical prompt distribution? We have a big difference between short chat and long form summarization.
[03:53] Ethan: Absolutely. If you can upload a sample prompt set or a small replay we can feed it into a load harness. Preferably two slices: short-chat (<=256 tokens) and long summaries (>=1024 tokens).
[04:05] Priya: I'll get that uploaded to the shared drive today.
[04:08] Marcus: A quick note: our security team prefers customer-managed keys for PHI. What limitations should we expect?
[04:14] Ethan: With BYOK, some features like cross-region caching may be limited, and there can be extra latencies on key unwraps. We'll document tradeoffs.
[04:23] Jenna: To keep things concrete — proposal: 12-month extension, add EU dedicated pool equivalent to 0.5x your current committed capacity (to start), with option to expand after 60 days. Price amendment + preferred provisioning window in return. Thoughts?
[04:40] Tomás: That sounds reasonable, product wants to start small.
[04:44] Priya: Yes, plus we want an exit/rollback plan if latency regresses.
[04:49] Jenna: We'll include a canary/rollback policy for the rollout: start with 10% traffic to EU + 90% to US, measure p99 and error rates, then ramp.
[04:58] Daniela: Also need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest, and whether log redaction is supported.
[05:04] Lara: Yes, encryption at rest + in transit is standard; log redaction — we have options to scrub prompt fields and send only aggregated analytics. We'll include redaction options in the security doc.
[05:16] Priya: On SLA, do we get a latency SLA or just uptime?
[05:20] Ethan: Our SLAs are uptime-focused; we offer latency SLO guidance and can include latency-oriented runbooks as part of enterprise support but not a strict p99 latency SLA today.
[05:31] Marcus: If we need stricter latency guarantees, what's the path?
[05:34] Ethan: Typically tying to Dedicated capacity plus colocated region and higher support tier is the path; plus local caching/prefix caching reduces reactive token cost and latency.
[05:45] Tomás: For procurement, legal wants an amendment we can sign quickly. What docs will you send?
[05:50] Jenna: We'll send: term amendment draft, pricing sheet for committed capacity, SOC2 summary, and technical checklist for EU provisioning. Also a short runbook for rollback.
[06:01] Priya: Can we get rough numbers today? Even rough monthly committed spend?
[06:05] Jenna: We can send ranges today; exact numbers after Ethan's benchmark to size the pool. Expect a few percent of uplift in committed monthly spend to secure priority and region allocation.
[06:14] Daniela: Is there a way to pilot private with a small windowed dataset first? We want to validate on de-identified PHI.
[06:21] Ethan: Yes, we can do a private pilot with de-identified subset in a VPC-peered hosted setup to validate keys and network without full on-prem install. That usually shortens risk.
[06:31] Tomás: OK. Timeline check: if we run benchmarks this week and confirm commitment, we can probably be live mid-April?
[06:37] Jenna: Mid-April is ambitious but possible if EU capacity is available. If not, earliest mid-to-late April. With commitment today we can prioritize.
[06:47] Priya: Let's say we commit by next Friday — what do we need to sign?
[06:52] Jenna: The amendment and a purchase order. We'll include language for provisioning SLAs and lead time.
[07:00] Marcus: One last infra Q: for burst capacity across regions, is there automatic fallback if EU pool is saturated?
[07:07] Ethan: Yes, we support smart routing: fallback to other compatible model variants in US or to hosted burst capacity. You can configure cost vs latency preference.
[07:19] Priya: Perfect. Any competitor notes — we ran a proof-of-concept with FastServe and they struggled with multi-tenant p99 under load.
[07:27] Jenna: Good to know. We'll make sure our benchmark covers that.
[07:32] Tomás: Ok let's recap actions.
[07:35] Jenna: Recap: Jenna send pricing + amendment; Ethan run EU benchmark and share traces; Lara share SOC2 + security artifacts; Marcus confirm VPC details; Priya upload prompt samples. We'll target a follow-up next week to review benchmarks.
[07:50] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[07:53] Jenna: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs today.
[07:56] (meeting ends)

Notes/Links referenced: pricing sheet (to be attached), EU benchmark harness (SE-run), SOC2 summary doc, example rollback runbook.

End of transcript.

Post-call recap (automatic): SE to run targeted load tests simulating Elmbridge prompt distribution; AE to propose amendment; CSM to coordinate security artifact handoff; schedule technical deep-dive as next meeting.
